Downing Street has backed calls for Fifa to investigate whether Argentina players broke rules by waving a banner in support of their country’s claims to the Falkland Islands, and insisted: “The World Cup might not be ours, but the Falkland Islands definitely are.”

An international row was sparked when Argentine players held up a banner that read ‘Las Malvinas son Argentinas’, which translates to ‘The Falkland Islands are Argentinian’, in the wake of their 2-1 victory over England in the World Cup semi-final.

Tensions between the UK and Argentina boiled over following the football clash, with Argentina accusing a British warship of an “illegal journey” into its waters, just hours after the victory.

But No 10 claimed the journey was in accordance with international law and said Argentina was fully notified of the ship’s movement, which was part of a “routine logistics visit to Chile”.

The prime minister’s official spokesperson said: “The World Cup might not be ours but the Falkland Islands definitely are.

“Our position is unchanged, self determination rests with the islanders. Our commitment to the Falklanders will never waver.”

She added that any action to be taken “rests with Fifa”, adding: “We’ve said throughout that politics should stay out of football”.

open image in gallery A banner was held up by some Argentine players after their win over England ( Getty )

The spokesperson also backed remarks from business secretary Peter Kyle, who had said the intervention from Argentina was “entirely inappropriate” and called for football’s governing body to investigate their actions.

“I saw the images this morning, and of course, it's entirely inappropriate”, he told Sky News. “Politics should stay away from football. That is a very clear principle of the World Cup, but any consequences that come from that is now a decision for Fifa.”

Speaking to the BBC, he added: “We expect Fifa to undertake an investigation into this. I think it was certain to happen because it was such an egregious violation of the rules of not having political activity as part of the football.”

The team could face disciplinary action and a fine for violating Fifa rules banning political messaging on the pitch.

Political tensions linger between Argentina and the UK over the Falkland Islands, which escalated into armed conflict in 1982 after Argentina invaded the islands.

Buenos Aires claims sovereignty over the Falklands, which are about 8,000 miles from Britain and 300 miles from Argentina.

Argentina vice-president Victoria Villarruel described England as “invaders” and “usurping pirates” in the build-up to the fixture, and tweeted a victory message at full-time that said “it wasn’t just another match”, alongside a video of what appeared to be Argentinian soldiers.

open image in gallery Sir Keir Starmer's official spokesperson hit back after Argentine football players wielded a politically charged banner ( AFP/Getty )

Later on Wednesday night, she shared images of the players holding the banner, along with a message which translated to: “The Falklands are Argentine! They banned bringing them to the stadium and forgot that we carry them in our blood and our hearts.”

The intervention came as Pablo Quirno, Argentina’s foreign minister, accused the Royal Navy of a “military incursion” into Argentine waters in a statement hours after the game ended.

He claimed HMS Medway, an offshore patrol vessel based in the Falkland Islands, had entered Argentina’s waters earlier in July without formally notifying the government. In his statement, he said a “formal note of protest” had been lodged with the British embassy to express “the strongest objection” to the action.

But No 10 hit back, claiming it had notified Argentina of the planned trip.

The prime minister’s official spokesperson said: "The facts here are that we notified the Argentinian government in advance of HMS Medway taking a routine logistics visit to Chile between 5 and 8 July to support British Antarctic survey operations, which will deliver essential stores and supplies to sustain scientific research in Antarctica.

“The Royal Navy always operates in full compliance with international law. Transit from the Falkland Islands to Chile was carried out by the most direct practical route considering operational safety and weather factors to ensure timely delivery."

Argentina, the defending World Cup champions, beat the Three Lions 2-1 in Atlanta.

Fans celebrated their victory, with some near the pitch holding a banner that read “Las Malvinas son Argentinas”. The banner made its way to the players, who held it up as they revelled in their win.

open image in gallery HMS Medway, one of the Royal Navy’s global patrol ships (LPhot Gareth Smith/MOD/Crown Copyright) ( MOD/Crown Copyright )

Their actions sparked furious backlash in England, with former army officer and ex-foreign and defence minister Tobias Ellwood telling The Independent: “Win or lose, do so with grace. This planned act wasn’t just about riling England, but about helping Argentina handle the humiliation of 1982 - which still hugely rattles the country today.

“Let’s ignore this pathetic stunt, leave Fifa to impose sanctions, and be proud of England’s World Cup performance.”

Meanwhile, Admiral Lord West – the former head of the Navy and the commanding officer of HMS Ardent, a frigate that was sunk in the Falklands conflict – said it was "pathetic child-like behaviour that we should ignore”.

“Although I hope Fifa take some disciplinary action", he added.

Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey called for Argentina’s players who celebrated with the Falklands banner to be suspended from the World Cup final.

“In August 2024 Rodri and Álvaro Morata were rightly banned for one match for singing ‘Gibraltar is Spain’. Now the Argentine players who celebrated with the ‘Falklands are Argentine’ banner must be barred from the final”, he said.

Education secretary Bridget Phillipson added: "To see that banner come out was really unacceptable and Fifa should be looking to take really firm action."

Falklands War hero Simon Weston, who was injured serving in the conflict during the bombing of the RFA Sir Galahad, said the players had “cheapened” their victory with the stunt.

He told The Independent that seeing the banner waved caused him “great sadness at the lack of professionalism, the lack of maturity of the Argentine players”.

“It also made me feel very sad for the Falkland Islanders, who have made it clear who they want to govern them. It’s not for others to tell people who they should align with. That’s called freedom; it’s called democracy,” he said.

Sir Sadiq Khan is to be given a peerage for his work as London mayor by outgoing prime minister Sir Keir Starmer.

A government source said: “Sadiq has been a brilliant mayor who has transformed London for the better, so this is thoroughly deserved.

“He has cut violent crime to record lows, cleaned up the capital’s air, delivered the Elizabeth Line, and got London building council homes again.”

Sir Sadiq will stay on as mayor and is not seeking a ministerial role, it is understood.

open image in gallery Sir Sadiq Khan has been made a peer as Sir Keir Starmer prepares to leave office ( Getty )

He is “honoured to be given a peerage”, a spokesperson for the mayor said. “London gave Sadiq the opportunities to go from a council estate to being Mayor of London, and his focus will continue to be ensuring that all Londoners get the same shot at reaching their full potential that London gave him and his family.

“Serving as mayor of the greatest city in the world continues to be the privilege of Sadiq’s life.

“He is excited about what more can be delivered in the years ahead and he will devote his time and energy to standing up for our city and building a fairer, safer and greener London for everyone.”

His peerage is part of a cross-party honours list understood to have been in the works before Sir Keir announced his resignation as PM.

There is also a peerage for June Sarpong, the television presenter, Christina McAnea, the former general secretary of the Unison union, one of Labour’s largest donors and Sir Chris Wormald, the former cabinet secretary who was ousted by Sir Keir earlier this year.

open image in gallery June Sarpong has been made a peer ( Getty )

Sir Ed Davey also welcomed five new Liberal Democrat peers announced in the list.

Agricultural economist Julia Aglionby, former Barnsley councillor and physiotherapist Hannah Kitching, economist Tim Leunig, Lib Dem campaigns director Dave McCobb and offshore wind entrepreneur Mark Petterson have been elevated to the House of Lords.

Sir Ed said: “Each of them has the right skills, experience and values to help us hold the government to account, deliver the change people need, and fix our broken politics, including reforming the House of Lords.”

Cities across Canada, the U.S. Midwest and East Coast are currently under thick blankets of wildfire smoke.

In Toronto, skies have been an apocalyptic orange since Wednesday morning and New York City, Detroit and Minneapolis were also facing severe air quality warnings.

The smoke is pouring south from more than 800 wildfires in the Canadian province of Ontario and elsewhere, destroying nearly 5 million acres and forced large-scale evacuations including in neighboring Minnesota.

For millions of North Americans, smoky skies are becoming a familiar sight in warmer months. In 2023, major cities including New York and San Francisco were being compared to the movie Blade Runner after the skies turned a burnt orange, blotting out the sun.

Just a decade ago, these events were fairly rare - so what is causing the onset of such ominous scenes?

open image in gallery Two people read a sign at a park as wildfire smoke from northwestern Ontario fills the sky in Toronto, Canada, on Wednesday. Hundreds of Canadian wildfires are sending choking smoke across provinces and into the U.S. ( REUTERS )

A new USA Today analysis of wildfire data over the past three decades revealed that the number acres burned each year is increasing. In short, wildfires are getting worse - but there’s a combination of factors that’s causing them to do so.

At the root is climate change, caused by humans continuing to burn fossil fuels and increasing the global temperature overall.

Climate change is bringing more frequent and severe extreme periods of heat and prolonged regional drought, setting up tinderbox conditions in forests that fuel larger, more erratic and stronger fires.

open image in gallery Smoke from Canadian wildfires fires pours eastward over Canada and the U.S. in this Tuesday satellite image from NASA. Wildfire smoke can travel hundreds of thousands of miles ( NASA Earth Observatory/Lauren Dauphin )

About half the smoke generated from wildfires between 1997-2020 could be linked to climate change, Loretta Mickley, an atmospheric chemist at Harvard University, told USA Today.

“If we zero in more recently from 2010 to 2020, those numbers increase,” she said.

Smoke from these fires can travel hundreds of thousands of miles and linger over areas for days, threatening human health.

Detroit, a city with 650,000 residents, had the worst air quality in the world Thursday, according to air quality tracking site iQAir, with Toronto coming second, and Minneapolis and Chicago ranking third and fourth.

Smoke in Michigan degraded visibility so much that the 26,372-foot Mackinac bridge was essentially invisible, forcing drivers to slow, according to UpNorthLive.

The air quality in all of these cities is considered to be hazardous to health. Impacts are forecast to last through Friday.

open image in gallery An aerial view shows smoke from Canadian wildfires over Chicago, Illinois, on Thursday. Wildfire smoke can bring decreased visibility that impacts transportation ( Getty )

Wildfire smoke contains particle pollution that’s been shown to negatively affect heart, brain and lung health.

“What we see after a big wildfire event is an increase in the rate of cardiac death, which is obviously very scary. We also see an increased need for rescue medicine for people with lung disease, and an increased need for people to visit their doctor in general because of some unexplained symptoms,” lung Dr. Erika Moseson told the American Lung Association.

Exposure for several days at unhealthy levels is considered to be the same as smoking about seven cigarettes a day if someone is outdoors the entire time, Stanford University says.

The negative impacts of wildfire smoke aren’t always immediate, either, with deaths occurring for up to three years after the fire has been put out.

open image in gallery Haze from Canadian wildfires blankets the Manhattan skyline on Wednesday in New York City. Wildfire smoke brings dangerous particle pollution that can harm the lungs ( Getty Images )

Children, seniors, people who are immunocompromised and pregnant women are the most at risk.

But there are steps people can take to protect themselves.

Wearing protective face masks, staying aware of the air quality levels and making sure all doors and windows are sealed tight are all good strategies to reduce exposure.

“When air quality is poor, limit time outdoors, avoid strenuous outdoor activities, consider exercising indoors and postpone or reschedule outdoor activities when possible.,” Dr. Farhan M. Asrar, of the University of Toronto, wrote in The Conversation Wednesday.

All teenagers should be offered a vaccine on the NHS to protect against meningitis B at around the age of 15, government advisers have recommended.

The advice by the Joint Committee on Vaccination and Immunisation (JCVI), which needs approval from the government, means youngsters should get a jab around the age of 15, with catch-up programmes for those who would otherwise miss out.

There have been a series of outbreaks of meningitis this year, the most serious in Kent, which left two teenagers dead.

The committee is recommending a booster jab around age 15 for those who had one as a baby (those born on or after May 1 2015). The first cohort this recommendation applies to will turn 15 in 2030. Children who missed the jab as a baby will be offered two doses.

In addition, JCVI says it strongly supports giving two doses of the meningitis B vaccine to children born on or before 30 April 2015. They would get this when they are around age 15.

This group were not offered the vaccine on the NHS as babies and so have missed out on protection as infants. Offering jabs when they hit their teens protects them when they are next most at risk.

Because it could take a while for any programme to be implemented, JCVI would also like a catch-up programme to ensure anyone who misses a vaccine does not lose out.

open image in gallery The vaccine is thought to offer protection for a few years ( PA )

The move by JCVI is separate to an announcement last month on a summer programme, which still stands.

Around a million Year 13 pupils and those under 25 starting university this autumn are being offered the meningitis B vaccine on the NHS this summer. This one-off jab programme offers two doses to youngsters aged 17 to 18 in Year 13, plus those aged under 25 going to university or other residential further education this autumn.

Young people are being offered their first dose from 20 July and a second dose will be given in August. Two doses, at least 28 days apart, are needed for full protection.

Meningitis is an inflammation of the protective membranes of the brain and spinal cord. Symptoms include a high temperature, cold hands and feet, vomiting, rapid breathing and skin changes such as paleness or a rash, which may be harder to see on darker skin.

Babies may also show irritability, a high-pitched cry, body stiffness or floppiness, and a bulging soft spot on their head.

The NHS says anyone concerned should seek immediate medical help rather than waiting for all symptoms or a rash to develop.

open image in gallery In March, students in Canterbury, Kent, queued to receive doses of the jab as the disease spread ( PA )

The outbreak in Canterbury, Kent, was the fastest growing and largest in the UK, and other smaller clusters of meningitis in young people since then have been bigger than expected.

The family of Juliette Kenny, 18, who died in the Kent outbreak, have been campaigning for teenagers and young people to be routinely given access to the meningitis B vaccine.

Close and prolonged contact in halls of residence, shared homes and at social events can increase the risk of contracting meningitis B.

Cases of meningitis B tend to peak in October to November each year.

But data suggests the meningitis B vaccine is highly effective, providing strong protection for at least five years after vaccination.

Wei Shen Lim, the committee chair, said: “We encourage everyone who is eligible to book an appointment online to receive the vaccine at a local pharmacy, in time for the second dose to be received before heading off to university or college.

open image in gallery The outbreak in Kent was classed as a ‘national incident’ ( Getty )

“For protection, two doses of the meningitis B vaccine are necessary, at least 28 days apart.

“Additionally, JCVI has now also provided government with a recommendation and additional considerations for a future routine meningitis B adolescent vaccination programme for those aged around 15 years.”

Shamez Ladhani, consultant epidemiologist at the UK Health Security Agency, has said previously the likely cause of more meningitis clusters this year is low population immunity against meningitis B.

“The most likely explanation is that we actually have had 25 years of declining cases of meningitis B disease,” he said.

“Now, meningococcal disease cycles go through cycles of 20 to 30 years.

“It goes down when you have good population immunity, and then that immunity goes down and new strains appear where the population doesn’t have immunity against these strains, and then cases start going up again.”

News.title: Reporter unfazed by cockroach crawling on her during live broadcast
News.content:
A KTLA reporter remained admirably calm as a cockroach crawled across her skin during a live broadcast.

Rachel Menitoff was discussing a heatwave in Southern California when the insect landed on her chest and proceeded to crawl across her neck.

Ms Mentioff finished off the report without paying notice to the cockroach, with the stations’ anchors praising her composure and professionalism.

“There’s no way I would’ve been able to keep my cool on this,” one said.

A later clip showed Ms Mentioff violently shaking her body and flipping her hair to make sure the creature had gone.

The Nike swoosh will be absent from the World Cup final, a stark indicator of rival Adidas's dominance on the tournament's biggest stage.

Argentina's semi-final victory over England on Wednesday extinguished the sportswear giant's hopes of sponsoring a team in Sunday's ultimate match.

Amid a fierce brand battle both on and off the pitch, the outcome represents a significant visibility boost for Adidas, which outfits both finalists: Argentina and Spain. Adidas had sponsored a total of 14 national teams in the tournament, while none of Nike's 12 teams, including semi-finalists England and France, managed to secure a spot in the final.

This outcome arrives as Nike grapples with years of steadily shrinking market share, having heavily relied on the tournament for a much-needed boost in sales and visibility.

The company signaled last month that CEO Elliott Hill's turnaround strategy faces significant obstacles, with persistent weakness in China and a cautious outlook overshadowing a modest fourth-quarter revenue beat. Nike's shares have lost nearly a third of their value this year as investors grow impatient with Hill's progress.

Argentina's semi-final victory over England on Wednesday extinguished the sportswear giant's hopes of sponsoring a team in Sunday's ultimate match ( Getty Images )

Morningstar analyst David Swartz underscored the deeper challenges facing Nike, stating, "There are more important issues, such as footwear innovation, inventory control, and stabilizing sales and margins in China." He added, "Adidas got more publicity, but that’s just the way it goes."

A Nike spokesperson maintained the company's long-term perspective, asserting that "our vision for football has never been tied to a single moment." Meanwhile, Adidas called the World Cup final a "proud moment" for the company, though it declined to share specific sales projections.

Despite its teams not reaching the final, Nike invested significantly in the tournament. It unveiled two new Mercurial soccer boots, partnered with local streetwear designers, and refreshed soccer merchandise at over 5,000 Nike and wholesale stores globally. Its "Rip the Script" World Cup campaign, featuring stars like Kylian Mbappe and Kim Kardashian, garnered 1.5 billion views in its first week, with national team kits selling 2.5 times more than during the 2022 Qatar World Cup.

However, Adidas, an official World Cup sponsor, has emerged as the "clear winner" in the athletic footwear and apparel market, according to Drake MacFarlane, a research analyst at M Science. Stronger momentum in the U.S. and Europe helped the brand gain share from Nike in the second quarter. While World Cup demand offered a lift, Adidas’ improvement extends beyond the event, whereas Nike continues to face pressure in Europe.

M Science data shows Adidas's share of the footwear market rose to 19.2% in June, up from 16.0% a year earlier, while Nike continued to shed share. Adidas executives reported robust bookings for World Cup products, totaling around 250 million euros (\$292 million) in the first quarter, with similar figures anticipated for the current quarter.

News.title: Police issue ‘do not approach’ warning after prisoner escapes from Manchester hospital
News.content:

Police are searching for a prisoner who escaped from hospital in Manchester.

Marwan Jumaa, 20, had been transferred from a secure hospital facility to North Manchester Hospital for medical treatment on Tuesday evening.

The prisoner, who is deemed to be a risk to himself and others, is serving a prison sentence for attacking two women.

Jumaa is believed to have links to Bury, Prestwich and Crumpsall in Greater Manchester, as well as Leeds and London.

Police have launched an urgent appeal for information and are warning the public not to approach him, but to call 999 immediately if they see him.

open image in gallery Jumaa had been transferred to North Manchester Hospital for medical treatment when he escaped ( GMP )

Jumaa is described as Black, about 5ft 10ins tall, and of skinny build with short dark hair.

Detective Chief Inspector Abigail Cronin, from Greater Manchester Police (GMP), said: “We are urging anybody to come forward who may have information about Marwan’s whereabouts.

“I recognise that this may heighten concern within the community. However, I want to assure you that we have officers working around the clock to find Marwan and return him to hospital as soon as possible.

“If sighted, do not approach him, please call 999 immediately, quoting log number 3544 of 14/07/2026.”

News.title: ‘I feel like I’m in front of a fireball’: 45C heat becomes India’s new normal
News.content:
Even under the shade of an umbrella, the fierce heat is unbearable. It’s nearing midday as Gulab Padiyar hammers yet another metal sheet into a simple bucket, but temperatures topped 40C hours ago.

“I feel like I’m in front of a gas stove – or a fireball,” Ms Padiyar says, perched on a once-white cushion beside a dusty road. “I feel like I’m cooking myself.”

The 53-year-old has little choice: it’s heat or hunger. Each day, Ms Padiyar earns around 400 rupees (roughly £3) making dozens of buckets – it’s just enough for her and her husband to survive.

“I feel dizzy and my eyes burn, sometimes I get headaches or faint,” she says. “But at the end of the day… this is the work I know, and others won’t employ me because of my age. So I think I have to continue, no matter how hot it gets.”

Ms Padiyar’s hometown, Ahmedabad, is no stranger to scorching temperatures. Home to roughly 8.5 million people, it’s the largest city in Gujarat – an arid state in western India where both Mahatma Gandhi and Narendra Modi, the country’s Prime Minister, were born.

But the mercury is rising. In the 1990s, the hot season between mid-March and mid-June averaged roughly 35 days above 40C, according to analysis from The Times of India. This year, that number hit 71. A study from the University of Oxford this month ranked Ahmedabad as the world’s second most “heat-risk city”, after Basra in Iraq.

Yet the Indian city has also been a trailblazer in extreme heat policy. Its experiences in the last 15 years offer strategies to adapt – and a warning about just how difficult that is, especially to protect workers in a “survival economy”.

News.title: Pound hits one-year high on hopes of Chancellor Mahmood
News.content:
The pound has hit a one-year high on hopes that Shabana Mahmood will be named Andy Burnham’s chancellor.

Sterling climbed 0.6pc against the euro to tip above €1.18, its highest level since June last year, after the Home Secretary emerged as the frontrunner to replace Rachel Reeves. Over the same timeframe, the pound rose as much as 0.8pc versus the dollar to more than $1.35.

Ms Mahmood is thought to be in pole position to take over from Rachel Reeves at the Treasury when Mr Burnham enters Downing Street on Monday, after weeks of speculation about his Cabinet choices.

Mr Miliband, the Energy Secretary, had previously been considered the top contender for No 11 after advising Mr Burnham, who won the Makerfield by-election last month, on his economic plans.

However, he is viewed less favourably by markets over concerns he will pursue a more Left-leaning agenda than rivals.

Philip Shaw, chief UK economist at Investec, said the pound had performed strongly against the euro and dollar as reports that Ms Mahmood was the frontrunner to become the next Chancellor were “soothing market fears of unduly lax fiscal policy”.

The rally for the pound also came as Britain’s economy returned to growth in May in a boost for incoming prime minister Andy Burnham.

The UK’s gross domestic product (GDP) rose by 0.1pc during the month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS).

It marked a rebound from a 0.1pc decline in April, which had been the first contraction in eight months.

Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics said the economy has been “more resilient” than previously thought but warned higher fuel prices would still restrain real incomes.

He said the 0.1pc rise in UK GDP in May “is not a bad welcome gift for incoming prime minister Andy Burnham”.

News.title: At the moment of reckoning, England’s old anxiety took hold
News.content:
All the years that have passed since those red shirts on a summer’s day at a long-gone Wembley Stadium – the humiliations, the occasional triumph, the plentiful servings of self-pity. For a short while in Atlanta it felt like that epoch might finally be ending and all it came down to was managing the last five minutes and whatever the beleaguered referee might add.

A place at a World Cup final was within England’s grasp, a mere 60 years since the last. But just as it loomed into view, already the players and their manager were tracing an old path. The man currently in charge of the England team might be German, the players might be of a generation finessed under bold new coaching ideas, but once more a familiar anxiety took hold. England were minutes from the prize. Yet team and manager were already obeying an old instinct to sabotage the moment.

England had been in retreat long before Lionel Messi served up for Enzo Fernández the goal that would level this World Cup semi-final, and then the second for Lautaro Martínez ,which would propel Argentina forward. Of course, Messi is Messi, and this Argentina team exist to exert his will on games by any means necessary. Yet, as ever, at the moment of reckoning, England demonstrated all the resistance of damp cardboard.

Thomas Tuchel once again reverted to the deep defensive position. Once again, the adapted five-man back line sat on the edge of their area. Against Mexico in the last 16, Tuchel was dismissive of any suggestion he had invited pressure, asking what other option he had with just 10 men. Against Norway in the quarter-finals he did the same, once Erling Haaland was off the pitch. Against Argentina, a team accustomed to playing with it all on the line, such a move was fatal.

News.title: Dengue outbreak complicates Bangladesh measles crisis response
News.content:
A major outbreak of dengue fever threatens to overwhelm hospitals in Bangladesh, where an explosive measles epidemic has already pushed the health system to the brink.

From the start of the year to the end of May, Bangladesh recorded 714 dengue cases and 1 death. By July 6, that had soared to 7,110 cases and 19 deaths.

Meanwhile more than 113,000 people have required hospital treatment for measles, with 718 of them dying, the vast majority among children under five.

Experts warn the dual crisis is putting more lives at risk.

“If you have a dengue outbreak that is already going to stretch public healthcare resources, and on top of that you have measles, this could become a huge burden, both on the resources and on the doctors and healthcare workers managing the patients,” Dr Ooi Eng Eong, a dengue expert and head of the Environmental Health Institute, National Environment Agency in Singapore, told The Telegraph.

Two diseases share enough symptoms to be mistaken for one another, with potentially fatal consequences.

“They present in a similar way, with fever and rash. It’s well documented that, in the past, measles cases have been mistaken for dengue, and dengue has been misdiagnosed as measles,” said Dr Eng Eong.

“Unfortunately, the treatment, especially to prevent progression to severe dengue, is quite different from how you would treat a measles case. So misdiagnosis could have quite important consequences for patients.”

News.title: Spain deliver footballing lesson to send France packing
News.content:
Whether you use your eyes or the underlying data, France and Spain look like the two best teams at this World Cup but only one of them will play in Sunday’s final in New Jersey.

France are the tournament’s top goalscorers with 16 goals in six matches, while European champions Spain have the best defence.

France have certainly played as a team at this tournament, but their great strength is a luxurious level of individual quality across a front four of Desire Doue, Michael Olise, Ousmane Dembele and Kylian Mbappe. Spain rely more on their collective patterns of play and a distinctive style which is very much their own.

Most opponents at this World Cup have sat off France and hoped to limit the damage, but Spain will not approach the game in that way which should make this an absorbing contest. Spain will want to hide the ball from France’s best players and ask questions of a defence which has been relatively untroubled.

However, the more possession Spain have, the higher up the pitch their centre-backs Aymeric Laporte and Pau Curbasi will be, which could leave them vulnerable to a fleet-footed France attack in transition.

If Spain are to hurt France, Lamine Yamal against either Theo Hernandez or Lucas Digne looks the most likely avenue. Left-back is the one position in France’s team in which they do not have an elite option.

Spain have been utterly dominant for long stretches of their matches, but have not converted that control into goals in the manner of France, and that could well be the difference. Mbappe is currently the tournament’s joint top scorer on eight goals, level with Lionel Messi and one behind Argentine in the all-time list of World Cup top scorers.

Messi, and England, will be watching this closely and it ought to be a cracker in Dallas.

News.title: Brainless batting seals England’s fate as India win first ODI
News.content:
It was a sporting wicket and England did not help themselves by picking the wrong side. They were a spinner too heavy and a seamer light. India could just motor through the middle overs once they averted losing wickets when the ball was hard, their only wobble was when Shubman Gill retired hurt for 80 but Washington Sundar and Axar Patel are old lags and saw India home with 28 balls to spare.

Edgbaston was full and gave the Blue for Bob charity a good send-off. This was the last money-raising day for prostate cancer in memory of Bob Willis after seven years raising £2m for prostate cancer research. Willis would have relished laying into some of England’s batting.

It is more than a decade since England relaunched their 50-over cricket at Edgbaston, scoring 408 against McCullum’s New Zealand and setting themselves on the path to World Cup glory. Then they were full of zest and new ideas. Something they have never replicated.

There are three survivors from that side still going. Of that trio, Root remains the most valuable and consistent. This innings took his career average over 50 and since making a hundred at the Champions Trophy last year he has averaged 70.

Jos Buttler scored a 77-ball 129 in that New Zealand game in 2015 and was a World Cup final hero four years later. This was his 200th ODI and Eoin Morgan presented him with a commemorative cap before play. Buttler’s 131 off 64 balls in the final T20 on Saturday was a reminder of what he can still do after a lean run but there are no guarantees he makes it to the World Cup in the same way that Root appears a rock-solid bet.

Buttler made five here and with other candidates to bat and keep, there might be a call for McCullum to make at some point down the line. Adil Rashid was the other survivor from that NZ ODI. He will be 39 at the next World Cup and you wonder if England may regret not giving Rehan Ahmed more experience. Rashid was milked, which generally happens when he plays India.

In 26-year-old Gurnoor Brar, India have found another strapping, punchy fast bowler who likes a battle, and after a wobbly start he struck twice in the 13th over – Jacob Bethell for a sticky 14 from 31, and Ben Duckett after a jaunty 43. Gill brought back Bumrah, he knocked over Brook with his first ball. Prasidh Krishna’s double-wicket maiden – Buttler caught off a leading edge and Sam Curran nicking behind – left England 80 for five.

Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez’s emotional letter begging Messi not to retire resurfaces 10 years on as pair combine to down England
Sports.content:
ENZO FERNANDEZ’s heartfelt message to Lionel Messi has resurfaced a decade after he first sent it.

The Chelsea midfielder scored a crucial equaliser on Wednesday night against England in their World Cup semi-final clash.



Messi provided the assist for the finish, minutes before clipping in another inch-perfect ball to Lautaro Martinez to secure Argentina a spot in the final.

The legendary attacker has absolutely stolen the show at this year’s tournament, marking eight goals and four assists in just seven appearances so far.



And the feat is made all the more impressive by the fact that he was weighing up retirement from international duty an entire decade ago.

The little magician announced his retirement from international football after his side lost the Copa America final to Chile in 2016.



But he went back on the decision just months later, with millions of distraught fans breathing a sigh of relief.

And among them was a 15-year-old Fernandez, who had penned an emotional message begging the icon to reconsider when news of his retirement first emerged.

The young star, who was then in Argentinian outfit River Plate‘s academy, wrote: “How are we going to convince you if in our lives we have never had 1 per cent of the pressure that you have on your shoulders?

“How are we going to convince you if we could not understand that you are a human being, a person with unmatched talent, the best player on the planet but a person anyway.

“Do what you want Lionel, but please think about staying. But stay to have fun, which is what these people have taken from you.

“In a world of ridiculous pressures, they manage to take away the most noble thing from the game. The fun.

“As a kid you probably dreamed of representing your country and having fun. Seeing you play in the Albiceleste is the greatest pride in the world.

“Play to have fun because when you have fun, you have no ideas how much fun we have. Thanks and sorry…”

Sports.title: ‘People think it’s brave… it’s not’ – Michael Owen blasts Thomas Tuchel over ‘pub team’ England tactics vs Argentina
Sports.content:
MICHAEL OWEN has likened Thomas Tuchel’s park-the-bus tactics against Argentina to that of a pub team.

In a scathing review of England’s semi-final exit, former striker Owen branded Tuchel’s ultra-defensive approach as “rubbish” and the opposite of brave.



England went 1-0 up against the reigning world champions in Atlanta on Wednesday through Anthony Gordon’s goal.

But Tuchel then tried to defend their way to victory, bringing on three defenders and giving momentum to their opponents.



It did not work as Lionel Messi created two late goals to break English hearts – and leave many viewers, including Owen, deeply frustrated.

Former Liverpool and Real Madrid forward Owen, 46, blasted: “Going back and dropping back and putting 11 men in your own box and just kicking it as hard as you can and heading it out and whatever, and taking a ball in the face, people think that’s brave. It’s not.

“It’s quite the opposite. It’s quite the opposite.

“Football isn’t about getting a ball in the nose and getting blood and everyone saying ‘Yeah that’s fantastic, yeah look how brave we are’.

“That’s rubbish. I can get my local pub team to do that.”

England had defended their way to a 3-2 victory against Mexico in the last 16.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

But that gritty display was praised because Tuchel’s side had ten men for most of the second half following Jarell Quansah’s red card.

Against Argentina, there was no man disadvantage.

Owen feels the way England were complimented for their win in the Azteca Stadium led to the defensive strategy against Messi and Co.

The ex-striker, who scored 40 goals in 89 games for England, including his wonderstrike against Argentina at World Cup ‘98, continued: “That’s where we lost the tournament, celebrating beating Mexico the way we did.

“It was the wrong way. The problem is, as a player, once that’s in your mind, (it’s like) ‘Ah we won. Everybody thinks we’re great and we did it doing this’.



“Subconsciously, as soon as you go 1-0 up now, what do you think we’re going to think? What do you think the players are going to think?

“And then the manager brings on three defenders, what message do you think that sends to Argentina?”

Sports.title: Lionel Messi savages England tactics in five damning words after sparking Argentina comeback at World Cup
Sports.content:
LIONEL MESSI tore England’s failed tactics to shreds with a scathing statement after Argentina knocked Thomas Tuchel’s men out of the World Cup.

Messi, 39, led the reigning world champions to their second consecutive final after a 2-1 win over the Three Lions on Wednesday in Atlanta, Georgia.



The Albiceleste came from behind late in the semi-final after the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner set up Enzo Fernandez’s equaliser on 85 minutes and Lautaro Martinez’s winner in the second minute of stoppage time.

England boss Tuchel, 52, came under intense scrutiny following his team’s heartbreaking elimination as his players sat back after Anthony Gordon’s opener.



The German tactician also brought in three defenders in Ezri Konsa, Dan Burn and Nico O’Reilly, while hooking Declan Rice and Gordon.

Messi didn’t hold back when addressing the ex-Chelsea boss’ controversial call that denied England their first World Cup final since 1966 when they beat West Germany at Wembley.



The Inter Miami superstar stated these tactics showed “they didn’t want it anymore”.

Messi said: “We felt a lot of emotion, and when we were drawing, we needed the support of the fans, because we saw that we could win it in 90 minutes.

“Because we already had the goal, because we entered through the inside, the outside, because we created opportunities with crosses, through line passes, through the inside.

“And we felt they didn’t want it anymore and we just kept coming, that’s why after the 1-1, the crowd helped us again once more, and as I said, we are happy because it was a close match.

“We always want to win, and also because it takes us to play another World Cup final.”

England legend Wayne Rooney slammed Tuchel’s mindset after the final whistle, with fellow BBC pundits Alan Shearer, Micah Richards and Joe Hart adding to the criticism.

The ex-Paris Saint-Germain boss explained he made defensive substitutions because he wanted to “close the spaces” and win more aerial duels.

And England captain Harry Kane admitted the performance against Argentina was “not enough”, especially “at this level”.

Kane said: “We played a good game ​for the large majority of it. Once we went 1-0 up, we seemed to just ​try and hold on.



“At this level, it’s not enough, so just gutted, gutted because we’ve worked so hard to be here and the lads have given every last bit of ​running, sweat, blood, tears, whatever it is.

“After the goal, whether it was them putting ​more men forward or us just not being able to match them man for man, it just ‌was wave ⁠after wave and we were trying to hold on as we were putting blocks in.

“But in the end, it wasn’t enough.”

Sports.title: Former England manager tipped to replace Mauricio Pochettino as USA boss after World Cup loss to Argentina
Sports.content:
A FORMER England manager has been tipped to replace Mauricio Pochettino as USA head coach in the wake of their World Cup exit.

The Three Lions crashed out of the tournament on Wednesday night after a stunning late comeback from Argentina in their semi-final clash.



It was a brutal defeat reminiscent of previous England tournament exits under iconic former manager Gareth Southgate.

And now Southgate is being tipped to make a return to the international scene and take over as USA head coach.



It comes as the future of current head coach Pochettino hangs in serious doubt.

He was linked with a move to AC Milan ahead of the World Cup and his contract with US Soccer is due to expire at the end of the tournament.

However, AC Milan ultimately went with Ruben Amorim over Pochettino and several other options have since been struck off the board.

Should Pochettino still depart, ESPN believes that Southgate could be their next best move.

Since he resigned from the England post after Euro 2024, Southgate has kept a low profile and focused on other opportunities.

He currently serves as a UEFA technical observer and also lectures at Harvard Business School.



Whether he will return to the soccer arena remains to be seen but his track record was particularly good with England.

During his eight-year tenure, Southgate brought back a consistency and belief that had been missing from the national team for a long time.

He led the Three Lions to the 2018 World Cup semi-finals and back-to-back European Championship finals in 2020 and 2024.

A particularly persuasive factor to lure Southgate would have been his relationship with US Soccer sporting director Matt Crocker.

However, Crocker left for a position with Saudi Arabia right before the World Cup in a major blow for the federation.



Crocker previously worked closely with Southgate at the English FA as the Head of Development.

Sports.title: Argentine golfer recreates Enzo Fernandez’s World Cup goal celebration against England after birdie putt at The Open
Sports.content:
ARGENTINE golfer Mateo Pulcini taunted England by recreating Enzo Fernandez’s goal celebration at The Open.

The amateur, 25, is the lone Argentinian in the field at Royal Birkdale this week.



And he made his presence known with an audacious celebration after holing a long putt for birdie on the 18th green.

When the ball dropped, Pulcini turned to the stands and put a hand behind each ear.



Hours earlier, Argentina midfielder Fernandez had done exactly the same thing after scoring from range in a 2-1 win over England in the World Cup semi-finals.

The crowd on Merseyside failed to cotton on as they met Pulcini’s gesture with an even louder cheer.



Pulcini hinted prior to his opening round that he was planning to twist the knife if Argentina dashed England’s World Cup dreams.

He said: “We’re already thinking about our plan on Thursday if we win, so, I need to ask the R&A if I can do… some stuff. We’re thinking.

“As soon as we beat Switzerland all of my friends texted me saying I had to do something if we beat England.”

Eerily, Pulcini also predicted a 2-1 win for Argentina.

Sports.content:
England's hopes of World Cup glory are OVER thanks to a stunning Enzo Fernandez strike and Lautaro Martinez's injury-time header as Argentina book their place in the final vs Spain

England's World Cup hopes are over after they fell short against reigning champions Argentina in Atlanta on Wednesday night.

Thomas Tuchel's men led 1-0 with five minutes of normal time remaining thanks to Anthony Gordon's goal, but defensive changes and an inability to keep possession proved crucial as a stunning Enzo Fernandez effort and an injury time header from substitute Lautaro Martinez sent Lionel Messi and co into another final.

On a night where both national anthems were booed by opposing supporters and Argentina players celebrated post-match with a flag that declared 'The Falklands belong to Argentina' England stars were left gutted by their failure to reach Sunday's final against Spain.

It was a night where Tuchel's substitutions badly backfired and a number of key men were NOT at their best, with Wayne Rooney pointing the finger of blame squarely at the Three Lions boss.

Despite calls for him to vacate his post, Tuchel has vowed to continue with England for the remainder of his contract - which will see him through until Euro 2028. He said: "We keep on going with the contract until the home Euros. I'm looking forward to that even though right now it's difficult to look that far ahead."

Follow all the fallout and reaction to England's semi-final defeat below...

Sports.title: The 31 dirty tricks Argentina used against England - full comprehensive list
Sports.content:
The 31 dirty tricks Argentina used against England - full comprehensive list

England bowed out of the World Cup semi-finals after a dramatic defeat to Argentina, who pulled out just about every trick in the book to advance

View 5 Images Argentina got away with a string of curious decisions in their World Cup semi-final win over England (Image: Getty Images)

England's World Cup quest came to an agonising close after Argentina came from behind to knock them out in the penultimate stage. However, Lionel Scaloni's side will contest Sunday's final against Spain having used every tool at their disposal.

‌



When all is said and done, the onus lies with Thomas Tuchel and his men for not doing enough to get the job done in Atlanta. After all, they would have been within their rights to fight fire with fire and deploy the same dark arts as their opponents.

‌



That doesn't make it any easier to swallow a particularly bitter pill, however. And it becomes that much more difficult to accept when breaking down the sheer quantity of underhanded offences Argentina were guilty of en route to a 2-1 comeback win.

‌



What did you make of Argentina's dirty tactics? Did they cross the line, or is all fair in love and war? Have your say below!

1 min

Alexis Mac Allister catches Elliot Anderson after pressing him just 19 seconds into the semi-final.

2 mins

Tensions rise when Leandro Parades unnecessarily shoves Jude Bellingham in the back, prompting the Real Madrid man to respond verbally, with players from both sides getting involved.

‌

11 mins

England players start to retaliate when Fernandez escapes punishment for another foul on Anderson before a brief grappling match on the floor.

At the same time, a recovering Morgan Rogers is tripped.

Following an offside flag against Simeone, Jordan Pickford collides with him while attempting to retrieve the ball, prompting the midfielder to flick his boot towards the England keeper.

15 mins

Sports.title: England World Cup player ratings: Bellingham shines but Arsenal duo suffer after gruelling season
Sports.content:
Here are England’s player ratings from the World Cup.

Let’s not forget this squad reached only England’s third semi final since winning the World Cup in 1966, and produced one of the most epic away displays in the Three Lions history, with their Estadio Azteca triumph against co-hosts Mexico.

There were some standout performers across the seven games that mattered. But some players could also have done a lot better.

And that, sadly, is a reflection of England’s tournament.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

ENGLAND PLAYER RATINGS

Jordan Pickford

The high point was Mexico but this was not vintage Pickford. He made the defence nervous with the ball at his feet. He did not look assured. Could he have done better on Enzo Fernandez’s equaliser against Argentina? I thought that was unstoppable but in previous tournaments, we didn't even question him.

Interesting times ahead with James Trafford eyeing No.1.

‌



Rating: 6

Reece James

His tournament highlights that it is hard to rely on him because of his fitness record and it is hard to argue he was at his best when he played. He missed too much of the tournament to say his inclusion was a success.

England need a more reliable right back.

‌



Rating: 6

View 7 Images Reece James injury issues reared their head again

Ezri Konsa

Blimey, what a kick in the teeth that he did not start the semifinal having played so well in the previous games.

‌



Thomas Tuchel loves him for his tenacity, reading of danger and he showed all of those things. Good, often underrated defender.

Rating: 7.5

John Stones

The two-on-one break against Norway was peak John Stones. People who criticise Alexander Sorloth miss the point. Stones gave him nowhere to go. It was incredible defending.

‌



Having missed much of the season, he was rusty and yet, unlike James, his inclusion was fully justified. Someone is going to get a hell of a free transfer. An England great.

His dressing room prank was a belter, too.

Rating: 7.5

Marc Guehi

‌



It was a shock when he was left out of the opening game against Croatia. And, frankly, sometimes by not playing, your value to the team becomes clearer. It did with Guehi.

So calm, classy and composed. You can see why Man City went all out for him. He has a long England career ahead. Class act.

Rating: 7.5

View 7 Images Marc Guehi celebrates England's win against Mexico (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Nico O’Reilly

Mixed bag. Not sure he ever hit the heights he reached with Man City last season but was solid and decent.

He was unlucky to get dropped a couple of times but that was a reflection of a lack of cohesion on the left plus a reminder that he is not actually a natural full back.

Rating: 6

‌



Dan Burn

Dan Burn summed it up. If I don’t come on, he said, then England are on the way to the World Cup final. Sadly, he came on. Heroics in Mexico (when we never thought he’d get a minute) and as a last-gasp substitute. But more cult figure than class.

We love Burn because it gives everyone hope. That’s lovely - but patronising all at the same time.

Rating: 6

‌



Jarell Quansah

Defined by his red card in Mexico. Moments like that can cost your team and if you lose then you are the villain. He is a good player, classy defender, a good centre-half.

But not a right back.

Rating: 5

‌



View 7 Images Jarell Quansah was sent off for this challenge on Mexico's Jesus Gallardo

Djed Spence

Played the game of his life against Argentina. And made brilliant substitute appearances against Croatia and Norway.

What a boost this can give his confidence, career and his future. His tackle late on against Argentina - which he celebrated as if he had scored - was iconic. Sad that he got cramp just when Lionel Messi popped up. Spence v Messi. No-one would have dreamed that before the World Cup.

‌



Rating: 8

Elliot Anderson

Good tournament. Completed a £116m move to Manchester City midway through and suddenly he put a few of the doubts about his price to bed. You are worth what someone is willing to pay. He is top class.

Good passing, incredible energy and unstoppable engine. He has enhanced his reputation big time.

‌



Rating: 8

View 7 Images Elliot Anderson reacts to England's World Cup exit - but he had a fine tournament (Image: Getty Images)

Declan Rice

His game against Mexico was hugely impressive. But, let’s be clear, the guy was running on empty - especially after getting food poisoning in Mexico.

‌



He needs a bloody good holiday. Not his best tournament but never lets England down.

Rating: 7

Jordan Henderson

Made history by becoming the first England player to play at a men’s World Cup. Finished it by breaking his arm after falling over advertising hoardings.

‌



One that he will want to forget. Good for morale.

Rating: 5

Jude Bellingham

Where to start? England’s best player by a mile. He is a national treasure, reminded us what it means to play for England and dominated games.

‌



What a tournament he had. Outstanding. All that pre-tournament nonsense about him not being a team player. He gave everything for the team.

His levels were off the charts. His performance in Mexico was the best I’ve seen in the flesh from an England player. His run of games the best since the lads of 66.

Rating: 9.5

View 7 Images Jude Bellingham scored six goals for the Three Lions (Image: Richard Pelham, Getty Images)

‌



Morgan Rogers

A bit-part player really but actually enhanced his standing. His assist for Anthony Gordon’s goal in the semi final. His shot parried by the keeper to set up Jude Bellingham in the quarter final.

Made a difference every time he came on. His assist justified his inclusion against Argentina.

Rating: 7

‌



Eberechi Eze

Did not get many opportunities but I really liked him against Norway when he changed England’s midfield dynamic.

A good inclusion overall. And you also feel he’d be such a good guy to have around the place.

Rating: 6.5

‌



Bukayo Saka

I regard Saka as one of England’s top three players. He’s so consistent, so reliable and so good.

This was not Bukayo Saka. He was miles off being fit.

He pushed himself at the end of the season to help England over the line. Arrived unfit - and finished needing a holiday. England in a semi final and not using Saka is unthinkable. That shows how much he has been struggling.

‌



Rating: 6

Should England sack Thomas Tuchel? Have your say in the comments section.

Noni Madueke

‌



Really disappointing tournament. Best from the bench but really arrived with low confidence despite winning the title with Arsenal.

He really needs a summer reset. There’s talent there but he can’t keep getting into positions and wasting crosses.

Rating: 5

Marcus Rashford

‌



Thomas Tuchel made it clear that he likes Rashford but the winger rarely produces on the pitch what he delivers in training.

Another unfulfilled tournament. He’s got so much talent. But we rarely see it for England.

Rating: 5

Anthony Gordon

‌



Frustrating at first and then grew in stature. He also delivered the best interview of the World Cup when he talked about overcoming the odds and proving himself. He did just that.

He scored against Argentina, played well as a forward and covered as a defender. Grew as a player and as a person.

Rating: 7.5

View 7 Images Anthony Gordon scored England's opener against Argentina (Image: Sebastian Widmann - FIFA, FIFA via Getty Images)

‌



Ollie Watkins

Six minutes against Panama. Never really got a fair crack - even when Harry Kane looked shattered. Impossible to mark fairly.

Rating: N/A

Ivan Toney

‌



Was it worth it? It didn’t feel like it. I think he deserved more minutes. Instead last gasp against Argentina was too little too late.

Rating: N/A

Harry Kane

England’s Captain Marvel did well overall but was poor against Argentina - when they needed him most.

‌



But after six goals and great leadership, it’s impossible to be critical. Set records, scored and led by example. What a top player and leader.

Rating: 9

Non-playing members: James Trafford, Dean Henderson, Trevoh Chalobah, Kobbie Mainoo

Sports.title: England star 'was not smart' in pivotal Argentina incident that VAR failed to help with
Sports.content:
EXCLUSIVE: England star 'was not smart' in pivotal Argentina incident that VAR failed to help with

England suffered a 2-1 World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina on Wednesday evening, with fans left wondering why VAR didn't intervene in key moments of the match

View Image Djed Spence was seemingly fouled by Lionel Messi (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

Djed Spence could have potentially kept England in with a chance at World Cup glory, had he been 'smarter' in the build up to Lautaro Martinez's winning goal for Argentina on Wednesday evening, says Glen Johnson. The Three Lions crumbled almost instantly after taking the lead in the 55th minute of the match at the Mercedes-Benz Stadium through Anthony Gordon.

‌



Rather than looking for a comfortable two-goal cushion, Thomas Tuchel's men were quick to sit in a low block and try to defend a 1-0 lead.

‌



However, with around 40 minutes left to play (including extra-time) that was always going to be too big of a task, considering Argentina's versatility on the front foot.

‌



Chelsea take instant action over Enzo Fernandez post as Argentina crush England hopes READ MORE :

Mark Chapman flies home from World Cup as BBC host misses final round of matches READ MORE :

Enzo Fernandez drew his nation level with five minutes left to play, with a silky finish from the edge of the area after being afforded acres of space by John Stones, Jude Bellingham and Morgan Rogers.

Martinez then popped up with the winner two minutes into stoppage time, beating Stones and Ezri Konsa at the back post to header home a 2-1 semi-final win.

However, as Argentinian players wheeled off in celebration, there were claims of foul play from England players directed toward referee Ismail Elfath. Alexis Mac Allister started the move when he was denied by the post from the edge of the area - the ball rolling toward the near side of the pitch.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Spence and Lionel Messi then raced toward the loose ball, with the England full-back making clean contact in a bid to clear any danger. However, Messi appeared to catch Spence's foot with his trailing boot in the process, with the defender immediately showing discomfort by hopping on one leg.

From there, Messi collected the ball on the flank, before whipping it in for Martinez to head into the back of Pickford's net from point blank range.

‌

Many England fans were quick to ask why no VAR intervention took place due to the apparent foul on Spence, considering Egypt had a goal chalked off against the World Champions for a similar incident in their quarter-final clash.

‌



And according to ex-England defender Johnson, who racked up 54 caps for the Three Lions during his professional playing career, it could come down to Spence not milking the collision more. Speaking exclusively to Mirror Football via Bovada, Johnson said: "Credit to Djed for getting back to his feet.

"Sometimes you need to be smarter. I do think we sometimes to need to match teams for the way they set up, the way the are aggressive to stamp our mark on the game.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Article continues below

"Maybe we’re a but too nice at times and if Djed goes down then it gives VAR a decision to make. But he gets on his feet and maybe that’s why no VAR was given and no other English player appealed. So not Argentina bias for me."

As a result of the loss, England will now be tasked with France in a third-place play-off match come Saturday, July 18. Argentina, meanwhile, take on Spain in the World Cup final the following evening.

Sports.title: Arsenal strike £34million transfer agreement for Greek winger Christos Tzolis
Sports.content:
Arsenal strike £34million transfer agreement for Greek winger Christos Tzolis

Arsenal have agreed a deal to sign one of Mikel Arteta's top targets after Leandro Trossard's exit was confirmed

View 3 Images Arsenal are plotting a £34m move for Christos Tzolis. (Image: Isosport/MB Media/Getty Images)

Arsenal have reportedly reached an agreement with Club Brugge to sign winger Christos Tzolis for £34million. The 24-year-old, formerly on the books of Norwich City as a teenager, is set to complete his permanent move to the Emirates Stadium in the coming days.

‌



Mikel Arteta has been monitoring Tzolis for several months and moved for the Greece international after Leandro Trossard's deal to join Besiktas was finalised. The Belgian, 31, is heading to Turkey in a £18m deal, freeing up the Gunners to sign Tzolis.

‌



He is expected to put pen to paper on a long-term contract, having already agreed personal terms with the Premier League champions. According to The Athletic, Arsenal will pay a flat £34m fee for his services after striking an agreement with his team Club Brugge.

‌



Their report claims the move is in the process of being finalised, with Tzolis giving his priority to joining the north London outfit after attracting interest from other clubs. Despite moving to sign a left-winger, it is not likely to affect the Arteta and sporting director Andrea Berta's pursuit of Aston Villa's England international Morgan Rogers.

Arsenal had initially targeted Juventus starlet Kenan Yildiz to solve their problems on the left flank. However, the Serie A rebuffed their enquiry for the Turkish winger, 21, and the Gunners moved onto other targets.

Arsenal news: Viktor Gyokeres swap transfer plan as Julian Alvarez signing becomes priority READ MORE :

Inside Man City plan to beat Arsenal and Man Utd to £85m transfer for World Cup star READ MORE :

Tzolis, who was under contract until June 2029, enjoyed a phenomenal campaign with the Belgian giants. He registered an incredible return of 22 goals and 29 assists in 51 appearances in 2025/26, including goals against Atalanta and Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

‌



Crystal Palace were keen on signing Tzolis last summer after selling Eberechi Eze to Arsenal. However, they were priced out of a move and eventually captured Yeremy Pino from Villarreal.

His first spell in England came back in 2020 when he signed for Norwich from PAOK, but struggled to make an impression in his 30 appearances for the Canaries. He had loans with FC Twente and Fortuna Dusseldorf before joining the German side in January 2024.

View 3 Images Christos Tzolis played against Arsenal in the Champions League (Image: Peter De Voecht / Photonews via Getty Images)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Tzolis then moved to Brugge just six months later where he found his feet. He has won 34 caps for Greece, scoring nine goals for the Euro 2004 winners.

Tzolis becomes Arteta's third summer signing, following Piero Hincapie's loan move being made permanent and the arrival of free agent Ilan Meslier, who was released by Leeds United. The Spaniard is expected to launch more high-profile moves this summer as he looks to successfully defend their title, having ended a 22-year wait for domestic success.

‌



One of the crucial members of their title-winning squad has already sealed his departure after Arsenal confirmed Trossard's departure earlier this week. In a statement, they said: “We can confirm that we have reached an agreement with Besiktas for the permanent transfer of Leandro Trossard.

View 3 Images Leandro Trossard is joining Besiktas from Arsenal

“With a transfer fee agreed, Leo, 31, has been granted permission to travel to Istanbul to undergo a medical and complete the formalities of his move to the Turkish Super Lig club. We will provide a further update once the transfer has been completed.”

Article continues below

Tzolis is now expected to complete his move subject to a medical and signing his contract. If it all goes ahead without a hitch, he could join his new team-mates for Arsenal's pre-season friendlies, which begins with a game against Girona on August 1.

Sports.title: Chelsea take instant action over Enzo Fernandez post as Argentina crush England hopes
Sports.content:
Chelsea take instant action over Enzo Fernandez post as Argentina crush England hopes

Enzo Fernandez played a key part as Argentina enjoyed a 2-1 World Cup semi-final win over England but some fans were left fuming with Chelsea's decision during the match

View Image Enzo Fernandez was instrumental in Argentina's win against England (Image: Shaun Botterill, Getty Images)

Chelsea were quick to remove a social media post pertaining to Enzo Fernandez during Argentina's 2-1 win over England at the World Cup, after a wave of online backlash. The 25-year-old clawed his nation back into Wednesday evening's semi-final encounter in Atlanta, Georgia, after the Three Lions took a second-half lead through Anthony Gordon.

‌



Fernandez found himself in heaps of space on the edge of Jordan Pickford's area, before unleashing with venom with just five minutes left to play. The ball curled and dipped past the England goalkeeper, as Fernandez wheeled away in animated fashion.

‌



Lautaro Martinez then shattered the dreams of Three Lions players, staff and fans watching worldwide, as he met the ball with a towering header at the back post two minutes into stoppage time to give the South American's a 2-1 lead, and ultimately, the match.

‌

The Blues shared a photograph of the midfielder cupping his ears in celebration, with the caption: "Enzo Fernandez," alongside an emoji of an explosion.

However, that move didn't sit well with England fans. Waves and waves of social media users were quick to comment on the post with messages of criticism, to the point that Chelsea made the decision to delete it altogether.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel told FIVE 'facts' about England vs Argentina as his decisions are ripped apart
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel told FIVE 'facts' about England vs Argentina as his decisions are ripped apart

Former Premier League boss Alan Pardew slammed Thomas Tuchel's decisions for England against Argentina

View 3 Images Thomas Tuchel has been criticised by Alan Pardew (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Former Premier League boss Alan Pardew has unleashed a withering breakdown of where England manager Thomas Tuchel went wrong against Argentina. The Three Lions suffered a painful 2-1 semi-final defeat after surrendering a second-half lead.

‌



England opened the scoring through Anthony Gordon in the 55th minute, but a succession of defensive substitutions gifted the initiative to Argentina. Enzo Fernandez levelled the match with five minutes remaining before Lautaro Martinez clinched the win for the defending champions in added time.

‌



Pardew has managed 318 Premier League games across five clubs, notably coaching Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni during his time at West Ham United. The 64-year-old utilised his experience to deliver what he labelled an "FA report" on England's performance.

‌



The former Newcastle United and Crystal Palace boss pulled no punches in his assessment of Tuchel's errors on Wednesday night, which cost England a place in the World Cup final. During an appearance on talkSPORT's Hawksbee and Jacobs show, Pardew broke his verdict down into "five facts".

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Pardew's first point was a relatively encouraging one, as he claimed Tuchel had set up his team to play "positive" football. He believed that the three changes made to bring Morgan Rodgers, Djed Spence and John Stones were "justified".

‌



"Argentina looked rattled and overhyped," Pardew said. "The referee was poor and was so lenient with continuous fouling. The first half was intriguing, actually, and Anderson around Messi had worked, although disgracefully, he got the first booking.

"The second period, we remained the same up until we scored from a long Harry Kane pass into a vacant channel that I suggest was a tactical decision. Our reaction to that goal was poor. Argentina fuelled by a desire to push and work us over. " His remaining four points all centred on Thomas Tuchel's tactical shortcomings.

‌



Fact two: "Had Scaloni covered the faults made by Mexico and Norway when England had taken the lead? And the answer to that is emphatically, yes he would have. I worked with him. There's no way he wouldn't have gone over those facts.

View 3 Images Alan Pardew listed what he believed Tuchel got wrong against Argentina (Image: YouTube/@talkSPORT)

"They worked the backline by overloading the sides, now putting dipping crosses into our box and working shooting from the edge. Goalie and post saved us before breakthrough."

‌



Fact three: "72 minutes, three offensive changes by Argentina, which you would expect. We changed Konsa for Gordon. Right there was our biggest mistake. No offensive substitution at that time. Playing a semi-final, and we didn't use Saka, by the way, who was fit, to give us an outlet. So no tactical tweak to control possession and clear our box."

View 3 Images Lionel Scaloni (R) played under Pardew at West Ham (Image: Ben Radford/Getty Images)

Sports.title: Tzolis: Arsenal's new 'warrior mode' winger - and perfect Trossard replacement
Sports.content:
In Christos Tzolis, Arsenal's first outfield signing since becoming Premier League champions is a fairly surprising one. But nobody will be more stunned about this deal than Norwich fans.

In 2021, Tzolis became the Canaries' record signing for £10m, played just 30 times in two years in an injury-hit spell, then left without a trace.

He even made his Premier League debut for Norwich at the Emirates in that September, when Arsenal were bottom of the table and without a point under Mikel Arteta in 2021.

Now he's back in England and joining the Premier League champions, having got 51 goal contributions in 52 games last season for Club Brugge.

Yet Tzolis is set to arrive at Arsenal as a record-breaker. At £34m, he will be Greece's most expensive player and the Belgian Pro League's biggest export.

But he also arrives as Leandro Trossard's direct replacement. And a closer look at Tzolis' profile shows a lot of similarities between the two players.

The first is the profile. Through those who know him, the Greek forward is a winger but like Trossard, he is also a No 10. Last summer, Crystal Palace strongly considered Tzolis as a replacement for now-Arsenal star Eberechi Eze.

Image: Tzolis is predominantly a left winger but can also play as a No 10

"He's able to fulfil different roles," Hayk Milkon tells Sky Sports, who was Club Brugge's assistant manager for Tzolis' entire time in Belgium up until February of this year.

"Coming from the left side - giving him this space to start wide and then find the moments to get more inside - that's where he's at his strongest.

"If he's assigned to play really wide to get these one-on-ones, he's able to do it. But he's always strongest the closer he is to the goal. Whenever he's more central, you can expect him at any moment to attack the space."

Another similarity between Tzolis and Trossard is their availability. Trossard had an exemplary injury record at Arsenal and was only injured for four matches in three-and-a-half-years. All of those four games came in his final season in north London.

Image: Tzolis played against Arsenal in the Champions League last season

Tzolis, meanwhile, had a similar record at Club Brugge. The longest he ever spent on the sidelines he had at the Belgian club was two matches - despite being one of the most energetic and intense players on the team.

"He's a guy that works a lot," adds Milkon. "He runs a lot of kilometres in the game, but also at high speeds and his sprint distance.

"Anyone can do that once in a week. He was doing it every three or four days with the Champions League. And his performances stayed stable."

A final comparison between Trossard and Tzolis is a slight temperament - bred from a desire to win. Arteta once called affectionately Trossard "a bit of a moaner" at Arsenal through his constant complaining in training and to referees.

And one of Tzolis' big areas of improvement, according to his former coach? "Emotional stability," says Milkon.

"He doesn't like to get kicked. Nobody likes it, obviously. But he doesn't. He's targeted very often. You need to stop him somehow. And the opposition were not able to stop him.

"But when he gets those kicks or when referee decisions are poor for him, then it might get a little bit difficult for him to stay in the game."

It is called "warrior mode," according to Milkon. And while Tzolis has that slight temperament, it does not translate to toxic or being a bad team-mate.

When Club Brugge were crowned Belgian champions in the season just gone, team-mates joined Tzolis in a classic Greek Sirtaki dance on the champions podium - showing how he grabbed the hearts and minds of the dressing room.

"They did this quite often," adds Milkon. "And you don't do it with a guy that is not so loved in the group.

Image: Tzolis' goals fired Club Brugge to the Belgian Pro League title last season

"As a person, he's an amazing lad. He makes the team like a family because he's so open, so easy going, always smiling, always making jokes in the dressing room, relaxed outside of the pitch.

"But when we go on the pitch, he's immediately in warrior mode. And every single training session is to win. It's not to just play around. And if he doesn't succeed in things, he might sometimes try to force it.

"But, yeah, he's a winner. And outside the pitch, he's just the most amazing guy that you can have in a dressing room.

"He might seem sometimes a little bit stubborn, but he is open. He is willing to learn. He has his way and his feelings on the pitch, of course, and you need to respect that.

"But when you give some instructions and you show him why he should do things, he's always open because he wants the best."

Does Gyokeres form prove Tzolis' goal numbers require scrutiny?

Obviously, what helped Tzolis win over the Club Brugge dressing room was his goal record, with 22 goals and 29 assists across all competitions last season.

But this was not a one-off season, as he has scored at least 20 goals in each of his last three campaigns at Brugge and Fortuna Dusseldorf.

His ball-striking ability was perfected in Belgium. "In the training sessions, you see immediately his powerful strike that he has," says Milkon.

"He always uses this quality to eliminate the goalkeeper because it's so powerful. It's unbelievable. But we managed to add the precision to that."

But of course, those goal numbers should be scrutinised due to the league they are being played in. The Belguim Pro League sits as the eighth strongest league in the world, according to Opta's Power Rankings - one place below the EFL Championship.

Arsenal discovered last season that Viktor Gyokeres' goals in Portugal were more difficult to translate into the Premier League - his 39 league goals for Sporting CP became 14 top-flight strikes in his debut Arsenal season.

Data from the Champions League, which is a fairer way of understanding Tzolis' potential, presents the Greek winger in a better light.

The 24-year-old was one of the most shot-friendly players in the Champions League last season, sitting in great company in most shots per 90.
